notes: Table 0 is a single price-list export: one row per SKU and one price entry per product, so /prices has one element per row.
SKU values appear as 00470001–00470012 in the source; preserve them as strings with leading zeros despite the profiler's int type.
Currency varies by row (6 SGD, 6 USD); keep each row's own currency and do not convert FX.

Tax included is explicitly 'No' for every row, so vat_included is false; Tax rate is explicitly 5%, yielding vat_rate 0.05. These are fixture values from the source, not inferred business conventions.

No effective_to column exists, and no status, barcode, brand, category or inventory columns are present; those optional targets should remain absent rather than fabricated, with contract defaults (status active) applied only as documented defaults.
The date column has an ambiguous_date hint, but the header format '(DD/MM/YYYY)' and the operator's explicit DD/MM/YYYY instruction resolve it to 3 April 2026.

tables.reason: One row per product SKU with a single net price, currency, sales unit, price list, VAT fields and validity date. This is a standard price-list export, not stock, promotions or category data.

columns.name: SKU
columns.reason: Header SKU, unique across all 12 rows, values 00470001–00470012. Unique product identifier; source displays leading zeros even though the profiler typed it as int, so it must be emitted as text preserving the zeros.

columns.name: Product name

columns.name: Currency

columns.name: Sales unit
columns.reason: Header Sales unit, constant value PCS, matching the sell-unit enum hint. unit_normalize maps PCS to canonical PCS.

columns.name: Price list
columns.reason: Header Price list with constant value 'standard' on all rows; operator confirms 'standard' is explicitly stated, so it maps directly to the price list name.

columns.name: Net price
columns.reason: Header Net price, numeric, never empty, distinct per row and ranging 1234.56–1356.77. This is the price amount for the row's price-list entry.

columns.name: Tax included
columns.reason: Explicit Yes/No column; all 12 rows are 'No', meaning the net price is VAT-exclusive. parse_bool gives false.

columns.name: Tax rate
columns.reason: Explicit Tax rate column, constant '5%' on all rows. Must be parsed as a fraction (0.05) via parse_number_th with percent_to_fraction. The 5% is a fixture value, not inferred from country or brand.

columns.name: Valid from (DD/MM/YYYY)
columns.reason: Header explicitly states DD/MM/YYYY and all rows contain 03/04/2026, i.e. 3 April 2026. The format label and operator instruction resolve the ambiguous-date hint, so parse day-first.

/currency mapped row by row (SGD/USD) via map_values with keep_unmapped; no FX conversion.
Collection dedupe keys set to the schema identity keys (/price_list, /effective_from); record-level dedupe on /sku.
Dropped the date-format open question — the header format and the operator instruction already resolve it.

No source evidence for /status, /barcode, /brand, /category, /description, /unit/pack_size, /prices/*/effective_to or any inventory/promotion rows: these stay unmapped (contract default status='active' is left to the schema) instead of being invented.
